transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately that brought you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. 

I guess what brought me in is... well, I'm just so worn out lately. I know everyone gets tired, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, but... it's gotten to where even just walking from my bedroom to the kitchen feels like I've been out hauling lumber all day. And I try to rest, I really do, but resting just doesn't give me anything back anymore. I just stay completely drained. 

I'm sorry, is that... is that the kind of information you need? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well... I try to keep a positive attitude, I really do. I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone down. But, um... yes, I suppose I have been feeling a bit low. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, at my age, but... I wake up with this, just this really heavy, hopeless feeling right in my chest. And... well, some days I just end up sitting out in the garage and... and I cry. I don't even know what starts it most of the time. I know I should be stronger than that, and I'm sorry to lay that on you. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for your notes.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood and the fatigue?

Well, um... let me think. I guess it's been... maybe about four months? 

I really don't want to make it sound like I'm blaming anyone, or making excuses. Especially not my wife, she's been so wonderful and I'm so proud of her. But it sort of started right around the time she went back to full-time work. I've just been spending most of the weekdays alone at the house since then. 

I know a grown man shouldn't struggle just because he's by himself during the day, and I feel a little silly even bringing it up. I should be able to handle my own company better than that. But... yes, about four months is when the heaviness really set in. 

Does that help? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline for your records.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, focus, or make decisions lately?

Oh, um... let's see. Thinking clearly? I... I think my mind is still working alright, thankfully. 

I try to do the crossword puzzle in the paper most mornings, just to... well, to make sure I'm staying sharp and not letting myself go completely. I don't want to be any more trouble than I already am. And since I'm mostly just around the house right now, I guess I don't have too many big decisions on my plate anyway. 

So, no, I haven't really noticed any real trouble with my focus or my memory. I hope that's an okay answer... I don't want to mess up your evaluation by not having all the things you're looking for. Is it alright that my focus is still doing okay?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or not wanting to live anymore?

Oh, um... well... I know I shouldn't think this way. I really don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for my life, or for my wife, because I'm not. I really try to appreciate everything I have. 

But... yes, honestly... the thought just keeps coming into my head that... that I should just be dead. It's a terrible thing to admit, and I feel so guilty even saying it out loud to you. I don't want to upset anyone. But sometimes, when I'm just sitting there all alone in the house... it actually scares me a little. Because I start thinking that... well, that I might actually do something to make that happen. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably very alarming to hear. I promise I don't want to cause any trouble or be a burden. I just... I wanted to be honest with you since you asked. Is it okay that I told you that? I hope I didn't say the wrong thing.
Have you ever felt like you might act on those thoughts or made any plans about how you would do it?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make you think less of me. I know I just said it, but... I don't have a, you know, a specific plan written down or anything like that. I wouldn't want to leave a mess for my wife to find. 

But... like I mentioned before, the thought just keeps coming back that I should just be dead. And... well, when I'm alone in the house during the day, it does scare me. Because my mind starts wandering, and I start thinking that... that I might actually do something to make that happen. I haven't bought anything or... or set a date, I promise. I'm just... I get frightened of my own thoughts sometimes. 

I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. I hope I'm giving you what you need for your assessment?
Have you ever felt that you might not be able to control the urge to act on these thoughts, or have you come close to doing something about them?

Oh, no, no... I promise I haven't let it get that far. I... I try very hard to keep everything under control. I haven't ever come close to actually doing anything, really. 

I know I just said the thoughts scare me, and they do, but... I just sit quietly until they pass. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm completely out of control or anything like that. I just sort of grip the armrests of my chair and wait it out. I'm trying to be good about it, I really am. 

I hope that's reassuring for you to hear? I really don't want to be a danger or... or make your job harder by being a high-risk case. I'm doing my best to hold it together. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with loved ones, don’t interest you as much anymore?

Well, um... I feel terrible admitting this, because I know people count on me, but... yes. It's true. I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or antisocial. I'm really not trying to be difficult.

It's just... I used to love doing so many things. I was always busy. I looked forward to my choir practice, and playing pickup basketball with the guys... I even liked working on cars and being the one to grill when the family got together. I really did enjoy all of that. 

But lately... I don't know what's wrong with me. I just can't seem to make myself care enough to show up to any of it anymore. I can't even bring myself to answer people's texts when they check in on me. I feel so guilty about it, ignoring everyone like that. I know it's not right. I just... I don't have it in me right now. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful. I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying all this. I'm really trying to get better, I promise. Is it normal to feel this way?
Have you ever felt this way before, with these same kinds of feelings, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?

Well, um... I really hope this isn't a bad sign, but... I don't think so? I mean, I've had times in my life where I was sad, you know, like when my dad passed away or when work was stressful, but... nothing like this. 

I've never felt this... empty before. And the thoughts and everything... it's all new to me. I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. I know it probably makes it harder to figure out what's wrong with me if there's no history of it, right? 

I promise I've been trying to think back, trying to see if maybe I just forgot feeling this way when I was younger, but... I really don't think I have. Is it okay that this is the first time? I hope that doesn't mean I'm just making a big deal out of nothing.

Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one where you felt persistently down, lost interest in things, or had similar struggles, even if it wasn’t quite as intense as what you’re describing now?

Well, um... I really don't think so. I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

I really can't recall ever feeling anything even close to this before. Like I said, I've had normal sad days, but... never a whole period of time where I just couldn't care about anything. I've always been a pretty upbeat guy, you know? Always trying to keep busy and help out. 

I hope it's not frustrating for you that I don't have a history of this for you to look at. I'm trying really hard to be helpful, I promise. I just... I don't have anything else to tell you about the past. I hope that's alright?
Before this current period, has there ever been a time in your life when you experienced a low mood or loss of interest that lasted for several weeks or more?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible because I know you've basically asked me this a couple of times now, and I really don't want to seem like I'm being uncooperative. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you. 

But... no, honestly. Even for just a few weeks, I've never felt this low or stopped caring about things before all this started. I really wish I could give you a different answer since it seems like maybe you're looking for one. 

Does it mess up your evaluation that I don't have any past history of it? I'm so sorry if I'm making your job harder by not having a better answer for you. I'm really trying my best to remember, I promise.
